blocks.heading: Choosing a protection strategy
blocks.text: Choose environmental protection by identifying the source, affected parties, severity, feasible alternatives and monitoring needs. A standard can require a result, an incentive can make cleaner methods more attractive and an extraction limit can constrain use of a finite stock. Compare effectiveness, cost and enforceability. Where a serious stated harm cannot be reduced adequately, restricting or postponing activity may be preferable to permitting it because it creates jobs. Where mitigation works, it may preserve useful production with less harm.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Tula Bricks can install a proven effective dust filter at a manageable cost. Nearby households currently face dust disturbance. Require effective control and monitoring rather than an unrelated measure or automatic closure. It directly addresses the harm while retaining output. The choice would change if the control could not prevent a severe stated effect.
